body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Monday, August 17, 2026, and we’re starting the week with a high near 99° and air quality at a moderate 58. Our top story this morning is the tragic wrong-way crash on Highway 99 that left three dead early Sunday. Let’s get you caught up on the night, the weather, and what’s ahead.

## The Kern Overnight

The night’s most serious incident unfolded around 1 a.m. on southbound Highway 99 north of 7th Standard Road, where a vehicle fire and extrication drew a heavy rescue response. Crews worked to free a pinned, unconscious subject from a burning vehicle; two patients were ultimately pulled out as green tags. Earlier, around 9:16 p.m., a palm tree fire spread to the roof of a two-story apartment complex on Spice Way off Villalobos Street. Engine 7 took incident command as additional units rolled in. Elsewhere, officers staged on a possible shooting call on Price Street that never developed on the air, chased a DUI driver in a white BMW fleeing east from the 33rd Street area, and handled a long string of low-stakes domestics and disturbances — including one at a Camellia Village apartment where a hole was punched in the wall.

## Today's weather

Today’s forecast calls for a high near 99° and a low around 73° tonight. It’s currently 81° at Meadows Field (KBFL). No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and air quality is holding at a moderate 58. We’re in for another warm August day, so stay cool and hydrated.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that three people died early Sunday morning in a wrong-way, three-vehicle crash on Highway 99.** According to CHP Bakersfield, a white Honda Accord traveling northbound in the southbound lanes collided with a white BMW 530i and a white Chevrolet Colorado north of 7th Standard Road around 12:44 a.m. The Honda caught fire, and all three occupants inside were killed. The BMW’s driver and one passenger sustained major injuries, while the Chevrolet’s two occupants had minor injuries. It is unknown if alcohol or drugs were a factor, and CHP is asking anyone with information to call (661) 396-6600.

**KGET 17 tells us that a man was arrested in a domestic violence standoff involving minors in Bakersfield.** Bakersfield Police Department said the incident began when officers responded to a domestic disturbance call. Upon arrival, they learned that a man had barricaded himself inside a residence with minors present. After a brief standoff, the suspect was taken into custody without incident, and the children were safely removed from the home. The investigation is ongoing, and no further details have been released at this time.

**Bakersfield Now announced that the 90s are back as a Pacific trough brings “cooler” highs to Kern County.** After a third heatwave, the region is seeing a slight dip in temperatures, with forecasts calling for highs in the 90s rather than the triple digits of recent weeks. While still warm, the change is a welcome relief for many residents and a reminder that even minor shifts in weather patterns can make a difference in daily life here in the valley.

## Something good

Kern County’s own Carlos Baldovinos, executive director of the Mission at Kern County, recently helped shape a federal best practices toolkit aimed at addressing addiction treatment within the homeless community. Baldovinos was among roughly 22 professionals from across the country who worked with the Trump administration, HUD, HHS, and the nation’s drug czar to develop the toolkit, which outlines best practices for working with individuals dealing with addiction. This initiative highlights local expertise contributing to a nationwide effort to address addiction — a true point of pride for our community.

## Coming up this week

Looking ahead, several public meetings and events are on the calendar for this week. On Tuesday, August 18, the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee meets at 12:00 p.m., followed by the Historic Preservation Commission at 4:00 p.m. and the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission at 2:00 p.m. On Wednesday, August 19, the Water Board convenes at 10:00 a.m. Later in the week, the Planning Commission gathers on Thursday, August 20, at 5:30 p.m. Meanwhile, the Fox Theater has a busy lineup of events, starting with Los Yonic’s Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio on August 22, followed by Rodney Carrington on August 27, CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE on August 28, Willie Barcena on August 29, and Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix, also on August 29. The month rounds out with the MI HISTORIA TOUR LEYENDAS DEL MARIACHI USA on September 4. Mark your calendars and stay tuned for more details on these events.
